locations.emptyBody: Add your first hotspot location to start deploying routers and selling internet packages.
locations.noRouters: No routers yet. Add one to get your captive portal link — no physical router needed to preview.
locations.name: Name
locations.noPackages: No packages yet. Add one so subscribers can buy internet on your portal.
locations.noSessions: No active sessions at this location.
locations.noSessionsHint: After re-pasting the router connection script, live “On router” status appears here. One seen MAC can still be a NAT gateway.
locations.onRouterHint: “On router” means the login is in MikroTik active hosts. A single MAC may still be a Pixlink/phone hotspot sharing with many devices.
locations.accessIntro: Simultaneous devices are controlled on each package. This location setting is only a fallback for vouchers when a package limit is missing.
locations.devicesHint: 0 = one device. Prefer setting Simultaneous devices on each package (e.g. 4 for family plans). Counts distinct Wi‑Fi MACs — not phones behind a home router in NAT/router mode.
locations.accessTip: Tip: use 1-device packages with a fair-use data cap, and discourage personal Wi‑Fi extenders in router mode on this hotspot.
locations.physicalHint: Hex / hAP — choose Existing or Create guest in Setup
locations.setupIntro: Two pastes on the MikroTik terminal. Test the portal with Preview portal anytime.
locations.existingHint: Hotspot must already assign IPs and show a login page. Script 1 only installs SpaiHub (walled garden, PAP, captive HTML).
locations.createHint: Add-if-missing guest network on LAN (10.10.10.0/24). Does not wipe WAN or wireless. Set your guest port below.

packages.intro: Choose how subscribers pay for internet access at this location.
packages.name: Package name
packages.timeDesc: Subscriber gets internet for a set browse time. Optional data cap.
packages.dataDesc: Subscriber gets a download allowance that must be used before expiry.
packages.uploadHint: Maximum upload speed per subscriber. Default is 1 MB/s.
packages.sharedHint: How many distinct Wi‑Fi MACs can use the same username and PIN at once. Use 1 for a single device, or 4 for a family package. Phones behind a home router in router/NAT mode still count as one MAC.
packages.durationHint: How long the subscriber stays connected after payment.
packages.fairUse: Fair use data limit (hidden from subscribers)
packages.fairUseHint: Buyers see unlimited browse. MikroTik still cuts the session when this cap is hit.
packages.fairUseOn: Enforced on the router for abuse prevention (shared with anyone on the same login, including tether/NAT). Subscribers still see unlimited data. SpaiHub does not use anti-tether firewall rules.
packages.fairUseOff: Leave unchecked for unlimited data during the browse period.
packages.allowanceHint: Total data the subscriber can download after payment.
packages.expiryHint: Unused data expires after this period.
packages.durationRequired: Browse duration must be greater than 0
packages.capRequired: Data cap must be greater than 0
packages.allowanceRequired: Download allowance must be greater than 0
packages.expiryRequired: Expiry period must be greater than 0

chr.title: MikroTik CHR onboarding
chr.prereqIntro: Before you start, confirm your CHR environment:
chr.prereq2: CHR can reach the SpaiHub API over HTTPS (outbound port 443).
chr.prereq3: Cloud firewall / security group allows egress to the internet.
chr.prereq4: CHR has no built-in Wi‑Fi — connect an AP or switch to the LAN bridge.
chr.seeDocs: See <docs>MikroTik CHR documentation</docs> for VM setup.
chr.warning: Run scripts in order on a fresh CHR or backup your config first. Verify interface names with /interface print.
chr.networkIntro: Default layout: WAN on ether1, LAN/AP on ether2, hotspot bridge at 192.168.88.0/24.
chr.bootstrapIntro: Paste this into the MikroTik terminal first. It creates bridge, DHCP, hotspot, and NAT.
chr.hotspotIntro: Run after bootstrap. Adds walled garden, SpaiHub profiles, and downloads hotspot/login.html to redirect clients to the captive portal.
chr.connectIntro: Run last. Starts heartbeat and command polling so SpaiHub can grant access after payment.
chr.waitingHint: After pasting all three scripts, the router should appear online within 1–2 minutes.
chr.check1: All three scripts pasted without errors
chr.check3: CHR can reach your SpaiHub API over HTTPS
chr.check4: Walled garden includes portal and API hosts from script 2
chr.connectedHint: Add packages at this location, then test the captive portal.
